keyVerseText: And saith unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
rootMeaning: The Greek noun πούς (poús) is a primary word in the language, with no known root derivation, indicating its fundamental nature in describing the part of the body known as the foot. Its literal sense encompasses not only the physical foot but also the lower leg from the ankle downward. This broad anatomical reference extends beyond the simple English term 'foot,' implying both the structural and functional aspects of the foot as a basis for movement and stability.
usageInScripture: Across its 93 occurrences, πούς is predominantly translated as 'feet' (63 times), highlighting its frequent plural use to denote the extremities used for standing and walking. It appears both in literal contexts, referring to the feet of men, beasts, or even birds, and in figurative senses, such as representing swiftness or motion. The translations 'footstool' and 'his feet' also appear, demonstrating the word's flexibility in describing physical position and symbolic authority or humility.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding πούς in its original sense enriches our grasp of biblical imagery related to movement, stability, and authority. The foot is often a metaphor for one's foundation or path in life, and its mention in Scripture can signify both physical presence and spiritual standing. The word's use in contexts like subjection under the feet or the footstool of God points to Christ's exalted position and the believer's humble submission. Recognizing the literal and figurative layers of πούς helps believers appreciate the depth of biblical teaching on Christ's lordship and our journey of faith.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 4:6 quotes Scripture to warn against testing God, saying angels will protect so one does not 'dash thy foot against a stone.' Here, πούς emphasizes the vulnerability and care involved in physical movement, symbolizing God's protective oversight. The word highlights the real danger and divine guardianship in the believer's path, reinforcing trust in God's providential care amid trials.
